# Git Commit & Branch Conventions — NurtureOS

> Auto-generated by `ai-sdlc-agents /sdlc:init` from the full commit history (12 commits at time of init) and current branches.
> **Adjust any section that doesn't match your team's intent.**

The repository follows **Conventional Commits**. There is **no ticket prefix** (no Jira/Linear in use).

---

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>: <short imperative description>

Optional body explaining *why*, not *what*.
```

### Rules

| Rule | Example | Anti-Pattern |
|------|---------|--------------|
| Start with a Conventional Commit type | `feat: add backend sync` | `Add backend sync` |
| Use `: ` (colon-space) after the type | `fix: sync race condition` | `fix - sync race`, `fix:sync race` |
| Imperative mood for the description | `Add`, `Fix`, `Rewrite`, `Expose` | `Added`, `Fixing`, `Rewriting` |
| Lowercase first word after the colon (matches existing history) | `feat: add production run scripts` | `feat: Add production run scripts` |
| No trailing period on subject | `fix: sync feedback loop` | `fix: sync feedback loop.` |
| Max 72 chars for the subject | Keep it concise | Long run-on sentences |
| An em-dash (`—`) is welcome for tail clauses | `fix: sync feedback loop — 16k requests in 9 mins` | — |

### Commit Types in Use

| Type | When to use | Example from history |
|------|-------------|----------------------|
| `feat` | New user-visible feature, new capability | `feat: dataset adapter for multi-file import` |
| `fix` | Bug fix, regression, race condition | `fix: backend sync missing monthPlans/yearPlans fields` |

Other Conventional types (`chore`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `perf`, `build`, `ci`) are allowed but unused so far. Use them when they genuinely fit; don't relabel a feature as `chore` to dodge changelog impact.

### Co-authored-by Trailer

When a commit is created with AI assistance (Copilot, Claude, etc.), add this trailer at the end of the body, separated by a blank line:

```
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

(Use the appropriate trailer for whichever assistant did the work.)

### Subject Verb Guide

Verbs actually used in this repo's history, sorted by frequency:

| Verb | When to use |
|------|-------------|
| `add` | Introducing something new (script, feature, hook, scaffold) |
| `rewrite` | Replacing an existing implementation wholesale |
| `expose` | Making something previously local available externally |
| `sync …` (no verb) | Acceptable for `fix:` subjects describing the broken subsystem directly, e.g. `fix: sync feedback loop` |

When in doubt, prefer a strong verb (`add`, `fix`, `rewrite`, `remove`, `simplify`, `extract`, `inline`) over weak ones (`update`, `change`, `improve`).

### Commit Body (Optional)

Use when the *why* isn't obvious from the subject. Separate from subject by a blank line. The repo's existing commits do not use bodies — that is fine for small changes but encouraged for incident fixes (the kind already documented in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`'s "Hard Bugs").

## Branch Naming

The history shows only long-lived shared branches:

```
develop   ← default integration branch
main      ← production / stable
```

There are no feature branches in the visible history (work has landed directly on `develop`). When you do create a topic branch, use:

```
<type>/<kebab-case-summary>
```

### Branch Types

| Prefix | Usage | Example |
|--------|-------|---------|
| `feature/` | New feature work | `feature/import-export` |
| `fix/` | Bug fix | `fix/sync-feedback-loop` |
| `chore/` | Tooling, deps, docs only | `chore/upgrade-vite-8` |
| `experiment/` | Throwaway spikes — squash or discard | `experiment/web-push` |

### Rules

- Always branch from `develop`, never from `main`.
- Keep branch names short and lowercase; use kebab-case.
- Do not include personal initials — the team is small and `git log` already shows author.
- Don't rebase or force-push `develop` or `main`.
- Delete topic branches after merge.

---

## PR Title

Use the same format as the commit subject: `<type>: <imperative description>`. When a PR is squash-merged, the resulting commit subject inherits the PR title — keeping the formats identical means the `git log` stays consistent.

If the PR contains multiple commits and is **merge**-merged (not squashed), the constituent commits should each follow the commit format above; the PR title can be slightly broader.

---

## Examples from History

**Good commits** (drawn from the actual log):
```
feat: NurtureOS V1 MVP — full project scaffold
feat: add backend sync + PWA registration + useSync hook
feat: import/export system with merge-safe preview
feat: dataset adapter for multi-file import
fix: backend sync missing monthPlans/yearPlans fields
fix: sync feedback loop — 16k requests in 9 mins
fix: rewrite sync — remove store subscriptions entirely
```

**Avoid:**
```
Update sync                          # no type prefix, no specifics
fix: stuff                           # no detail
fix: Sync feedback loop.             # capitalized first word + trailing period (inconsistent with history)
PROJ-123: add feature                # no ticket scheme is in use
WIP                                  # never land WIP commits on develop/main
```
